newsitem.title: USA: Pepsi sees $1.0 bln in gains over two years.
newsitem.headline: Pepsi sees $1.0 bln in gains over two years.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc may record as much as $1.0 billion in gains this year and next, the company's chief executive, Roger Enrico, told analysts on Wednesday, according to a PepsiCo spokesman.

At the meeting, Enrico did not specify the source of the gains, though they are likely to come from Wednesday's initial public offering of the company's New Zealand restaurant business and Pepsi's sale of its restaurant supply distribution business, spokesman Dick Detwiler told Reuters.

"Hetold analysts we have great flexibility in achieving mid-teens EPS growth from year to year, and we have about one billion dollars in one-time gains we could use to get to that growth," Detwiler said, paraphrasing Enrico.
Analysts at the meeting, however, were expecting year-to-year earnings growth from the company of about 15 percent without the extraordinary gains.
"The news about the gains took the street by surprise," said analyst Edward Froelich of Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette's Pershing division.
PepsiCo at the meeting also "made it very clear we have no plans to spin off our bottling business," Detwiler said.
The company said on Monday it would restructuring its bottling operations into a separate unit with its own management structure.
Analysts speculated at the time the move preceeded Pepsi spinning off the bottling business.
